sentences.text: This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode).
Heard learned counsel for the appellants, learned counsel for the State and learned counsel for the informant.

This is an appeal under section 14-A of S.C. & S.T. (PoA) Act, 1989 in connection with Special G.R.
Case No.65 of 2021 arising out of Gaisilat P.S. Case No.147 of 2021 pending in the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge, Padampur for offences punishable under sections 147/148/294/427/336/506/458/307/395/354/354-B/376-D/ 149 of the I.P.C. read with section 3(1)(r)(s)(w)(i)(ii) & 3(2)(v)(va) of the S.C. & S.T. (PoA) Act.

entities.text: Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge, Padampur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: // 2 // Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the appellants are in judicial custody since 13.09.2021 and when earlier the appellants approached this Court for bail, the bail application was rejected.

However, liberty was granted to them to renew their prayer for bail after examination of Umakanta Sahu vs State Of Odisha & Another on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21546717/
1

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the victim in the learned trial Court.
Learned counsel further submits that the victim has been examined in the learned trial Court as P.W.1 and at this stage, there is no chance of tampering with the evidence.
Therefore, the bail application may be favourably considered.
Learned counsel files the certified copy of the deposition of the victim, which is taken on record.
Learned counsel for the State opposes the prayer for bail and placed the evidence of the victim, who stated in her examination-in-chief that Banti, Nihar, Bablu and Shyama committed rape on her.
However, he fairly submits that the victim has not stated that appellant no.1 Umakanta Sahu committed rape on her.

Considering the submissions made by learned counsel for the respective parties, the evidence of the victim, while not inclining to release appellant no.2 on bail, I direct the appellant no.1 to be released on bail.

Let the appellant no.1 be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a bail bond of Rs.50,000/- (rupees fifty thousand) with two local solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Court in seisin over the matter with further conditions as the learned Court may deem just and proper with further conditions that he shall not try to keep any contact with the victim in any manner whatsoever, he shall not tamper with the evidence and he shall not indulge in any criminal activities and shall // 3 // appear before the learned trial Court on each date to which the case would be posted for trial.
Violation of any of the conditions shall entail cancellation of bail.
The CRLA is accordingly disposed of.
Issue urgent certified copy of this order on proper application.

(S.K. Sahoo) Judge amit Location: HIGH COURT OF ORISSA, CUTTACK Umakanta Sahu vs State Of Odisha & Another on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21546717/
